---- MODULE W4Od6m4p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Call, Car, MaxWait, NoCall, NoCar

ASSUME NoCall \notin Call /\ NoCar \notin Car /\ MaxWait \in Nat

VARIABLES waiting, carOf, jobOf, served
vars == <<waiting, carOf, jobOf, served>>

Idle(c) == jobOf[c] = NoCall

Init ==
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ carOf = [k \in Call |-> NoCar]
  /\ jobOf = [c \in Car |-> NoCall]
  /\ served = {}

Arrive(k) ==
  /\ k \notin waiting
  /\ carOf[k] = NoCar
  /\ k \notin served
  /\ Cardinality(waiting) < MaxWait
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carOf, jobOf, served>>

Withdraw(k) ==
  /\ k \in waiting
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carOf, jobOf, served>>

Dispatch(k, c) ==
  /\ k \in waiting
  /\ Idle(c)
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {k}
  /\ carOf' = [carOf EXCEPT ![k] = c]
  /\ jobOf' = [jobOf EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED served

Complete(c) ==
  /\ jobOf[c] # NoCall
  /\ LET k == jobOf[c] IN
       /\ jobOf' = [jobOf EXCEPT ![c] = NoCall]
       /\ carOf' = [carOf EXCEPT ![k] = NoCar]
       /\ served' = served \cup {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED waiting

Reissue(k) ==
  /\ k \in served
  /\ carOf[k] = NoCar
  /\ served' = served \ {k}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, carOf, jobOf>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Call : Arrive(k)
  \/ \E k \in Call : Withdraw(k)
  \/ \E k \in Call, c \in Car : Dispatch(k, c)
  \/ \E c \in Car : Complete(c)
  \/ \E k \in Call : Reissue(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoSharedCar ==
  \A c \in Car :
    jobOf[c] # NoCall => carOf[jobOf[c]] = c /\ jobOf[c] \notin waiting
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Call = {k1, k2, k3}
  Car = {a, b}
  MaxWait = 2
  NoCall = NoCall
  NoCar = NoCar
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoSharedCar
nl:
A skyscraper elevator bank receives hall calls from floors and must dispatch each call to exactly one elevator car. Pending hall calls sit in a bounded intake buffer; because calls and acknowledgements travel over a noisy bus they can be observed in any order, so the dispatcher is free to pick any waiting call rather than the oldest one. When the intake buffer is already full the building panel refuses to register a new call (backpressure) instead of dropping it silently. The dispatcher assigns a chosen waiting call to some car that is currently idle, recording both that the car now owns that call and that the call is bound to that car. A waiting call may also be withdrawn by the floor before it is ever dispatched. When a car finishes serving its call it becomes idle again and the call is marked served, and a served call may later be reissued as a fresh call. The bank must never let one physical car be committed to two different hall calls at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every moment each elevator car is the owner of at most one live hall call, so two distinct calls are never both bound to the same car.

---- MODULE W4Od0m9p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Surgeon, Room, MaxEpoch, None

ASSUME None \notin Surgeon /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES epoch, auth, cached, holds
vars == <<epoch, auth, cached, holds>>

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ auth = Surgeon
  /\ cached = [s \in Surgeon |-> 0]
  /\ holds = [r \in Room |-> None]

Sync(s) ==
  /\ cached[s] # epoch
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, auth, holds>>

Claim(s, r) ==
  /\ s \in auth
  /\ cached[s] = epoch
  /\ holds[r] = None
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![r] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, auth, cached>>

Release(s, r) ==
  /\ holds[r] = s
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![r] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, auth, cached>>

Reconfigure(newAuth) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ newAuth # {}
  /\ newAuth \subseteq Surgeon
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ auth' = newAuth
  /\ holds' = [r \in Room |-> IF holds[r] \in newAuth THEN holds[r] ELSE None]
  /\ UNCHANGED cached

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Surgeon : Sync(s)
  \/ \E s \in Surgeon, r \in Room : Claim(s, r)
  \/ \E s \in Surgeon, r \in Room : Release(s, r)
  \/ \E na \in SUBSET Surgeon : Reconfigure(na)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnauthorizedHold ==
  \A r \in Room : holds[r] # None => holds[r] \in auth
====

CONSTANTS
  Surgeon = {s1, s2, s3}
  Room = {r1, r2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedHold
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler is reconfigured in numbered epochs as staff rosters change through the day. A central coordinator holds the current epoch number and the set of surgeons authorized to hold rooms in that epoch. Each surgeon caches the epoch number it last learned; a slow surgeon may lag behind the coordinator but is never considered failed, and it catches up by synchronizing to the current epoch. A surgeon may claim a free operating room only while it is authorized in the current epoch and its cached epoch matches the coordinator's, and it may release a room it holds. When the roster is reconfigured the coordinator advances to the next epoch, installs a new authorized set, and immediately fences out any surgeon that is no longer authorized by clearing the rooms it was holding. The scheduler must guarantee that a room is never held by a surgeon outside the currently authorized roster.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every operating room that is currently held is held by a surgeon who belongs to the authorized set of the current epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Node, Seat, NoNode, Free

ASSUME NoNode \notin Node /\ Free \notin Node

VARIABLES holder, lock, wants, offers
vars == <<holder, lock, wants, offers>>

Init ==
  /\ \E n \in Node : holder = n
  /\ lock = [s \in Seat |-> Free]
  /\ wants = {}
  /\ offers = {}

Request(n) ==
  /\ holder # n
  /\ n \notin wants
  /\ wants' = wants \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, lock, offers>>

Grab(n, s) ==
  /\ holder = n
  /\ lock[s] = Free
  /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![s] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, wants, offers>>

Release(n, s) ==
  /\ lock[s] = n
  /\ lock' = [lock EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, wants, offers>>

Yield(n) ==
  /\ holder = n
  /\ \A s \in Seat : lock[s] # n
  /\ wants # {}
  /\ holder' = NoNode
  /\ offers' = wants
  /\ wants' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED lock

Claim(m) ==
  /\ holder = NoNode
  /\ m \in offers
  /\ holder' = m
  /\ offers' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, wants>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Node : Request(n)
  \/ \E n \in Node, s \in Seat : Grab(n, s)
  \/ \E n \in Node, s \in Seat : Release(n, s)
  \/ \E n \in Node : Yield(n)
  \/ \E m \in Node : Claim(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyHolderLocks ==
  \A s \in Seat : lock[s] # Free => lock[s] = holder
====

  Node = {n1, n2, n3}
  Seat = {a, b}
  NoNode = NoNode
  Free = Free
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyHolderLocks
nl:
A university course-registration system serializes access to a shared table of enrollment seats using a logical token that circulates around a ring of department nodes. Only the node currently holding the token may take edit-locks on seats, and it may hold several seat locks at once while it is editing. When a node wants a turn it records a request; when the holder is finished it must first free every seat lock it holds, then release the token by offering it to all outstanding requesters at once. Because these offers travel over a congested campus network they race and may be observed in any order, so whichever requester claims the offer first becomes the new holder and the remaining offers are dropped. While the token is between holders no node holds it. The essential requirement is that a seat lock is only ever held by the node that currently holds the token.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every seat that is currently edit-locked is locked by the one node that currently holds the token, so no node without the token holds any lock.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bus, Cap

ASSUME Cap \in Nat

VARIABLES load, shed, holder, ready
vars == <<load, shed, holder, ready>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN load[x] + SumOver(S \ {x})

Init ==
  /\ shed = Cap
  /\ load = [b \in Bus |-> 0]
  /\ \E b \in Bus : holder = b
  /\ ready = [b \in Bus |-> TRUE]

Restore(b) ==
  /\ holder = b
  /\ ready[b]
  /\ shed > 0
  /\ load[b] < Cap
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![b] = load[b] + 1]
  /\ shed' = shed - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ready>>

Shed(b) ==
  /\ holder = b
  /\ ready[b]
  /\ load[b] > 0
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![b] = load[b] - 1]
  /\ shed' = shed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ready>>

Pass(b, c) ==
  /\ holder = b
  /\ b # c
  /\ holder' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, shed, ready>>

Stall(b) ==
  /\ ready[b]
  /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, shed, holder>>

Resync(b) ==
  /\ ~ready[b]
  /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, shed, holder>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bus : Restore(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bus : Shed(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bus, c \in Bus : Pass(b, c)
  \/ \E b \in Bus : Stall(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bus : Resync(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LoadConserved ==
  SumOver(Bus) + shed = Cap
====

CONSTANTS
  Bus = {b1, b2, b3}
  Cap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed number of megawatt units distributed across several buses, plus a shed pool holding units that have been temporarily dropped from service. The total number of units in the grid is fixed: units are never created or destroyed, only moved between a bus and the shed pool. A logical token circulates among the buses, and only the bus currently holding the token may shed or restore units. A bus can be temporarily slow to respond and must resynchronize before it is allowed to act, but it is never considered failed and always recovers. The token holder may shed a unit from itself into the pool, or restore a unit from the pool back onto itself, and the token may be passed to any other bus. The absolute requirement is conservation: at every instant the units spread across all buses together with the units in the shed pool add up to exactly the grid's fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of megawatt units held across all buses plus the units sitting in the shed pool is always equal to the grid's fixed total capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od12m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Ticket, MaxBuf

ASSUME MaxBuf \in Nat

VARIABLES admitted, buf, applied, ready
vars == <<admitted, buf, applied, ready>>

BufSet == {buf[i] : i \in DOMAIN buf}

Init ==
  /\ admitted = {}
  /\ buf = << >>
  /\ applied = {}
  /\ ready = TRUE

Admit(t) ==
  /\ t \notin admitted
  /\ Len(buf) < MaxBuf
  /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {t}
  /\ buf' = Append(buf, t)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, ready>>

Apply ==
  /\ ready
  /\ buf # << >>
  /\ applied' = applied \cup {Head(buf)}
  /\ buf' = Tail(buf)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, ready>>

Stall ==
  /\ ready
  /\ ready' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, buf, applied>>

Resync ==
  /\ ~ready
  /\ ready' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, buf, applied>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Ticket : Admit(t)
  \/ Apply
  \/ Stall
  \/ Resync

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
  /\ applied \cap BufSet = {}
  /\ admitted = applied \cup BufSet
====

CONSTANTS
  Ticket = {t1, t2, t3, t4}
  MaxBuf = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker receives distinct update tickets (a donation logged, a unit dispensed, a correction) that must all be folded into a shared inventory record without any being lost. Incoming tickets are held in a bounded work buffer; when the buffer is full the intake desk refuses new tickets (backpressure) rather than dropping them. A single applier thread takes the ticket at the head of the buffer and folds it into the record, marking that ticket applied. The applier can be temporarily slow and must be ready before it processes a ticket, but it is never considered failed and always becomes ready again. Once a ticket has been admitted it is either still waiting in the buffer or already applied, and it is never applied more than once. The guarantee the bank depends on is that no admitted update is ever silently dropped or double-counted.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of admitted update tickets is exactly partitioned into those still waiting in the buffer and those already applied, with no ticket both waiting and applied.

---- MODULE W4Od16m4p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Rx, Bin, MaxQ, Empty, NoBin

ASSUME Empty \notin Rx /\ NoBin \notin Bin /\ MaxQ \in Nat

VARIABLES queue, occupant, placedIn, done
vars == <<queue, occupant, placedIn, done>>

InQueue(r) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = r

Init ==
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ occupant = [b \in Bin |-> Empty]
  /\ placedIn = [r \in Rx |-> NoBin]
  /\ done = {}

Arrive(r) ==
  /\ ~InQueue(r)
  /\ placedIn[r] = NoBin
  /\ r \notin done
  /\ Len(queue) < MaxQ
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, placedIn, done>>

Route(b) ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ occupant[b] = Empty
  /\ LET r == Head(queue) IN
       /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![b] = r]
       /\ placedIn' = [placedIn EXCEPT ![r] = b]
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED done

Collect(b) ==
  /\ occupant[b] # Empty
  /\ LET r == occupant[b] IN
       /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![b] = Empty]
       /\ placedIn' = [placedIn EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
       /\ done' = done \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED queue

Reissue(r) ==
  /\ r \in done
  /\ placedIn[r] = NoBin
  /\ done' = done \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, occupant, placedIn>>

AdminForce(r, b) ==
  /\ placedIn[r] = NoBin
  /\ ~InQueue(r)
  /\ LET prev == occupant[b] IN
       /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![b] = r]
       /\ placedIn' = [rr \in Rx |->
            IF rr = r THEN b
            ELSE IF rr = prev THEN NoBin
            ELSE placedIn[rr]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, done>>

AdminClear(b) ==
  /\ occupant[b] # Empty
  /\ LET r == occupant[b] IN
       /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![b] = Empty]
       /\ placedIn' = [placedIn EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, done>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Rx : Arrive(r)
  \/ \E b \in Bin : Route(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bin : Collect(b)
  \/ \E r \in Rx : Reissue(r)
  \/ \E r \in Rx, b \in Bin : AdminForce(r, b)
  \/ \E b \in Bin : AdminClear(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BinConsistent ==
  /\ \A b \in Bin : occupant[b] # Empty => placedIn[occupant[b]] = b
  /\ \A r \in Rx : placedIn[r] # NoBin => occupant[placedIn[r]] = r
====

CONSTANTS
  Rx = {p1, p2, p3}
  Bin = {c1, c2}
  MaxQ = 2
  Empty = Empty
  NoBin = NoBin
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BinConsistent
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser routes filled prescriptions into a bank of pickup bins, where each bin can hold at most one prescription at a time. Prescriptions ready for pickup wait in a bounded staging queue; when the queue is full no more prescriptions are staged (backpressure). A router takes the prescription at the head of the queue and drops it into some empty bin, recording both which prescription now sits in that bin and which bin holds that prescription. When a customer collects their prescription the bin is emptied and the prescription is marked collected; a collected prescription may later be reissued. A privileged pharmacy administrator can override the normal flow: the admin can force a specific prescription directly into a specific bin, evicting whatever prescription was there back to being unplaced, and can force-empty any bin. Throughout, no single bin may ever be recorded as holding two different prescriptions, and the bin-to-prescription and prescription-to-bin records must never disagree.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every bin its recorded occupant agrees with that prescription's recorded bin, and for every placed prescription its recorded bin agrees with that bin's occupant, so no bin is doubly allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od9m7p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Ctrl, Cap, Hi

ASSUME Cap \in Nat /\ Hi \in Nat /\ Cap =< Hi

VARIABLES reg, snap, goal, armed
vars == <<reg, snap, goal, armed>>

Init ==
  /\ reg = 0
  /\ snap = [c \in Ctrl |-> 0]
  /\ goal = [c \in Ctrl |-> 0]
  /\ armed = [c \in Ctrl |-> FALSE]

Snapshot(c) ==
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
  /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, goal>>

Aim(c, v) ==
  /\ v \in 0..Hi
  /\ goal' = [goal EXCEPT ![c] = v]
  /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snap>>

Commit(c) ==
  /\ armed[c]
  /\ reg = snap[c]
  /\ goal[c] =< Cap
  /\ reg' = goal[c]
  /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, goal>>

OperatorSet(w) ==
  /\ w \in 0..Cap
  /\ reg' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, goal, armed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Ctrl : Snapshot(c)
  \/ \E c \in Ctrl, v \in 0..Hi : Aim(c, v)
  \/ \E c \in Ctrl : Commit(c)
  \/ \E w \in 0..Cap : OperatorSet(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCapacity ==
  reg =< Cap
====

CONSTANTS
  Ctrl = {c1, c2}
  Cap = 2
  Hi = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A power-grid load shedder coordinates several regional controllers that all contend to update a single shared register holding the total committed shed level. The register must never be driven above the grid's firm capacity limit. Each controller works by first snapshotting the current register value, then arming a proposed new level, and finally attempting a compare-and-swap: the swap succeeds only if the register still equals the value it snapshotted and the proposed level is within capacity, otherwise the controller must snapshot again and retry. A privileged grid operator can override the register directly, but only ever to a level that is itself within capacity. Proposed levels may be aimed higher than capacity by a careless controller, and it is the compare-and-swap's capacity check that must reject them. The safety requirement is that the committed shed level in the register is never above the firm capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared register's committed shed level is at all times less than or equal to the grid's firm capacity limit.

---- MODULE W4Od8m4p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Inst, Job, MaxQ, None

ASSUME None \notin Inst /\ MaxQ \in Nat

VARIABLES pool, q, lockedBy, inCrit
vars == <<pool, q, lockedBy, inCrit>>

InQ(i, j) == \E k \in DOMAIN q[i] : q[i][k] = j

Init ==
  /\ pool = Job
  /\ q = [i \in Inst |-> << >>]
  /\ lockedBy = None
  /\ inCrit = [i \in Inst |-> FALSE]

Take(i, j) ==
  /\ j \in pool
  /\ Len(q[i]) < MaxQ
  /\ pool' = pool \ {j}
  /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![i] = Append(q[i], j)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lockedBy, inCrit>>

Cancel(i, j) ==
  /\ InQ(i, j)
  /\ ~inCrit[i]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {j}
  /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![i] = SelectSeq(q[i], LAMBDA x : x # j)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lockedBy, inCrit>>

Enter(i) ==
  /\ lockedBy = None
  /\ q[i] # << >>
  /\ lockedBy' = i
  /\ inCrit' = [inCrit EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, q>>

Exit(i) ==
  /\ lockedBy = i
  /\ lockedBy' = None
  /\ inCrit' = [inCrit EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {Head(q[i])}
  /\ q' = [q EXCEPT ![i] = Tail(q[i])]

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Inst, j \in Job : Take(i, j)
  \/ \E i \in Inst, j \in Job : Cancel(i, j)
  \/ \E i \in Inst : Enter(i)
  \/ \E i \in Inst : Exit(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

QJobs(i) == {q[i][k] : k \in DOMAIN q[i]}
AllQ == UNION {QJobs(i) : i \in Inst}

MutualExclusion ==
  /\ \A i \in Inst : inCrit[i] => lockedBy = i
  /\ pool \cap AllQ = {}
  /\ pool \cup AllQ = Job
====

CONSTANTS
  Inst = {A, B}
  Job = {j1, j2, j3}
  MaxQ = 2
  None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A university course-registration system runs two independent campus instances that both draw work from one shared pool of enrollment jobs. Each instance pulls jobs from the shared pool into its own bounded work queue; when an instance's queue is full it stops pulling (backpressure). To actually commit an enrollment a worker must enter a single shared critical section guarded by one registrar lock, and only one instance may be inside that critical section at any time. An instance enters the critical section only when the lock is free and it has a job queued, marking itself as inside; when it exits it releases the lock, dequeues the finished job, and returns that job to the shared pool so it can be processed again. An instance may also cancel a queued job, sending it straight back to the shared pool. The system must guarantee that the two campus instances never both sit inside the registrar critical section at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever an instance is marked as inside the critical section, it is the current holder of the registrar lock, so two instances are never inside the critical section simultaneously.

---- MODULE W4Od2m8p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Fleet, Shelf, Z1, Z2, None

ASSUME None \notin Fleet /\ Z1 \cup Z2 = Shelf /\ Z1 \cap Z2 = {}

Zones == {Z1, Z2}
ZoneOf(s) == IF s \in Z1 THEN Z1 ELSE Z2

VARIABLES pool, sealed, zlock, slock
vars == <<pool, sealed, zlock, slock>>

Init ==
  /\ pool = Shelf
  /\ sealed = {}
  /\ zlock = [z \in Zones |-> None]
  /\ slock = [s \in Shelf |-> None]

AcqZone(f, z) ==
  /\ zlock[z] = None
  /\ zlock' = [zlock EXCEPT ![z] = f]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, sealed, slock>>

AcqShelf(f, s) ==
  /\ slock[s] = None
  /\ zlock[ZoneOf(s)] = f
  /\ slock' = [slock EXCEPT ![s] = f]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, sealed, zlock>>

Seal(f, s) ==
  /\ slock[s] = f
  /\ zlock[ZoneOf(s)] = f
  /\ s \in pool
  /\ pool' = pool \ {s}
  /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zlock, slock>>

RelShelf(f, s) ==
  /\ slock[s] = f
  /\ slock' = [slock EXCEPT ![s] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, sealed, zlock>>

RelZone(f, z) ==
  /\ zlock[z] = f
  /\ \A s \in Shelf : (ZoneOf(s) = z => slock[s] # f)
  /\ zlock' = [zlock EXCEPT ![z] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, sealed, slock>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Fleet, z \in Zones : AcqZone(f, z)
  \/ \E f \in Fleet, s \in Shelf : AcqShelf(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Fleet, s \in Shelf : Seal(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Fleet, s \in Shelf : RelShelf(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Fleet, z \in Zones : RelZone(f, z)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SafeSealing ==
  /\ pool \cap sealed = {}
  /\ pool \cup sealed = Shelf
  /\ \A s \in Shelf : slock[s] # None => zlock[ZoneOf(s)] = slock[s]
====
nl:
A warehouse is worked by two independent robot fleets that share one pool of shelves, each shelf holding a single item, and the shelves are grouped into two zones. Performing the irreversible seal-and-ship action on a shelf's item requires taking two locks in strict hierarchical order: first the coarse lock on the shelf's zone, then the fine lock on the shelf itself, and a fleet may take a shelf's fine lock only while it already holds that shelf's zone lock. Once both locks are held by the same fleet it may seal the shelf's item, which permanently moves that shelf from the available pool into the sealed set. Sealing is irreversible: a sealed shelf never returns to the pool, so its item is sealed at most once. Fleets release fine locks and then zone locks, and a zone lock is released only once the fleet holds no fine lock inside it.
